## ⚠️ My recommendation above is amended by measurement — the condition I attached to it has fired

**Status of this reading:** from the in-flight draft PR #8261 (#8103's read-only half). The dev has **not** delivered its final report and I have **not** reviewed the diff, so this is reported as an incoming measurement, not as an accepted finding. I am posting it now anyway because this card sits in the maintainer's inbox with a recommendation whose stated precondition has just been contradicted, and leaving that standing would be the more misleading choice. ⚠️ Treat as provisional pending my ACCEPT.

### What was falsified

I wrote above that the recommendation was conditional on re-establishing #8063's three reachability facts, and that **"if any of those cannot be established, the answer should be A regardless."** One of the three came back **RED**:

| Fact | Reading |
|---|---|
| Handle ids minted per `encrypt()` call | GREEN |
| **`sys_setting.value_enc` is the only column holding a handle** | **RED — FALSIFIED** |
| Audit trail records digests, not handles | GREEN |

`sys_secret` reportedly has **three** producer paths, not one — and says so in its own schema (`platform-objects/src/system/sys-secret.object.ts`):

1. `SettingsService` → handle in `sys_setting.value_enc`
2. the engine's `secret`-field channel → `secret: id` on **an arbitrary business row**, including tenant-authored objects
3. the datasource credential binder → `sys_secret: id` at `external.credentialsRef`

Two are invisible from `service-settings`, and (2) is **not statically enumerable** — it is every `secret`-typed field on every registered object.

### Why this changes the decision rather than just informing it

A sweep that reads "unreferenced by `sys_setting`" as "unreferenced" **would delete live datasource credentials and live business-row secrets.** That is not a tuning risk on option C — it makes the naive form of **every** deleting option unsafe, B included, because B deletes exactly what the classifier names.

The PR's response is a third verdict value — `unattributable`, for rows that are unreferenced but not provably settings' — which is never reported as an orphan. If that guard holds up under review, a safe sweep is still *conceivable*, but only over the attributable subset, and that is a materially smaller and differently-shaped claim than the card was written against.

### A second inversion worth the maintainer's attention

The PR also reports that for this population the security framing in #8103 is **backwards**: after pre-fix rotations the value **still in force is the oldest one** — the credential the admin believed replaced — while the orphans hold the values the admin *intended* to set and which never took effect.

If that holds, **deleting the orphans does not retire the exposed credential.** The exposed one is referenced, so no sweep would touch it. The orphans remain real exposure (if the admin also rotated at the provider, the newest orphan may be currently valid), but the deletion sweep is no longer the remedy for the headline risk — which is most of the argument for doing it urgently at all.

### Amended recommendation

**A** (report-only for this release), with B reachable later and scoped to the **attributable** subset only. ⛔ **C is now clearly out** — an unattended boot-time delete-many over a table with two invisible producers, one of them not statically enumerable.

The four-edge face above stands; the *measured business pull* edge moves against urgency, because the exposure the sweep was going to close is not the one the sweep would touch.

⚠️ **Do not decide on this comment alone** — it reports a draft PR's claims. I will post the reviewed verdict when the dev's report is in, and correct this in public if review does not sustain it.

Measurement input from #8103's read-only half (PR #8261 — report only, no deletion). This card says the recommendation is *"conditional on a measurement that is not in yet"* and that **"if any of those cannot be established, the answer should be A regardless."**

**One of the three could not be established — it is false.**

| Fact | Reading |
| --- | --- |
| handle ids minted per `encrypt()` | ✅ re-established |
| `sys_setting.value_enc` is the only column holding a handle | ❌ **falsified** |
| audit records digests, not handles | ✅ re-established |

`sys_secret` has **three** producers, as its own schema states: `SettingsService`; the engine's `secret`-field channel, which stores `secret: id` on **any** business row including tenant-authored objects; and the datasource credential binder, which stores `sys_secret: id` at `external.credentialsRef`. There is no producer column on `sys_secret`, and `namespace`/`key` mean different things per producer. So a sweep keyed on `sys_setting` alone would delete **live datasource credentials and live business-row secrets**, and the engine's holder set is not statically enumerable — it depends on each instance's registered objects.

Two further readings that bear on the four-edge face:

1. **The exposure framing is inverted for this population.** Measured against a real engine: after pre-fix rotations the value **still in force is the oldest** — the credential the admin believed replaced — while the **orphans hold the values the admin intended to set**. Deleting orphans therefore does *not* retire the exposed credential. The orphans are still real exposure (if the admin also rotated at the provider, the newest orphan may be currently valid), but the "close the exposure" argument for option C is weaker than it reads.

2. **There is no recovery path for a wrong deletion.** Because the audit trail records digests and never handles, a row deleted in error cannot even be *named* afterwards, let alone restored. That sharpens the asymmetry-of-error argument this card already makes.

Option **C** is now measurably unsafe as originally framed. **A** is what the conditional in this card selects. **B** only becomes safe once a reference set spanning all three producers is built at runtime — which cannot be done from `service-settings`, since two of the three families are invisible there.

The landed classifier reflects this: rows it cannot attribute to the settings producer are reported `unattributable`, never `orphaned`.

## Blocker discharged — this card is now decidable

`Blocked-by: #8103` in the body above is **spent**. PR #8261 merged, so the measurements this decision was waiting on are in and reviewed.

The provisional reading I posted earlier (comment 5274762816) is now **reviewer-confirmed**, and I verified the load-bearing claim independently on `origin/main` rather than taking the dev's word: the engine's `secret`-field channel (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:4737`, invoked from three write paths) and the datasource binder (`sys_secret://…` at `external.credentialsRef` in `service-datasource`) both exist and are both invisible from `service-settings`. **Reachability fact 2 is dead.**

### Standing recommendation: **A**

Report-only this release. B remains reachable *later*, but only over the **attributable** subset and only after a reference union spanning all three producers exists — which cannot be built from `service-settings` and, for the engine's channel, is instance-specific (every `secret`-typed field on every registered object, including tenant-authored ones) and therefore not precomputable. ⛔ **C is out on measured grounds**, not on caution.

Two facts that hardened A since I first recommended it:

1. **`orphaned` is a heuristic verdict**, not a decision procedure — no producer column on `sys_secret`, and `(namespace, key)` means something different per producer. So even the bucket a sweep would target is not provably safe to delete.
2. **The audit trail records digests, never handles** ⇒ a row deleted in error cannot even be *named* afterwards, let alone recovered. The irreversible side of the asymmetry is worse than I stated originally.

And the inversion still stands: for this population the value **in force is the oldest one** — the credential the admin believed replaced — while the orphans hold values that never took effect. So a sweep does not retire the exposed credential. Most of the urgency argument for deleting at all does not survive that.

⛔ **Nothing is blocked on your answer.** The read-only half has landed; #8103 sits at `pm:blocked` against this card and will stay quiet until you rule. No nagging from this seat.

## Maintainer ruling — Option B (conditional)

Ruled by the maintainer in a live PM session, 2026-08-13 (session `session_015XyMgCSMGGn9oSwbQEeWYg`), verbatim: 「其他全部接受你的建议。」 — accepting the card's own recommendation as presented.

**Ruling: B — opt-in admin command, dry-run by default, explicit `--delete` flag for the destructive pass.** ⛔ C (unattended boot-time sweep) is rejected outright: the error asymmetry (missed orphan = pre-existing exposure persists; wrong deletion = in-force credential destroyed irreversibly) forbids running the irreversible side unattended.

**The condition stands as written:** this ruling activates only if #8103's read-only dispatch re-establishes the three reachability facts AND delivers a classifier that separates orphaned / in-force / legacy-inline / re-wrapped rows. **If any of that cannot be established, the outcome is A regardless** (report ships, no deletion ships, this card closes not-planned with the reason).

**Implementation notes (for when #8103 closes and the unlock scan re-prices this):**
- Destructive pass requires the human-initiated flag; default invocation must print the same report #8103 ships. An agent running the command without reading gets a report, never a deletion.
- Re-price against #8103's actual findings before dispatch — its measured population sizes the whole card.

Label swap: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:blocked` (`Blocked-by: #8103` already in the body) + `domain:services`.

## ⚠️ The ruling's own condition had already fired when the ruling was written — literal execution selects **A**, not B

Reading the ruling (comment 5278878841, 10:04:50Z) as written, not around it.

### What the ruling says

> **The condition stands as written:** this ruling activates only if #8103's read-only dispatch re-establishes the three reachability facts AND delivers a classifier that separates orphaned / in-force / legacy-inline / re-wrapped rows. **If any of that cannot be established, the outcome is A regardless** (report ships, no deletion ships, this card closes not-planned with the reason).

### The condition is a conjunction, and its first half is false

| Conjunct | Status |
|---|---|
| re-establishes **the three** reachability facts | ❌ **fact 2 FALSIFIED** |
| delivers the four-way classifier | ✅ delivered |

`sys_setting.value_enc` is **not** the only column holding a `sys_secret` handle. Three producers exist — `SettingsService`; the engine's `secret`-field channel (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:4737`, three write paths, storing `secret:<id>` on **any** business row including tenant-authored objects); and the datasource binder (`sys_secret://…` at `external.credentialsRef`). Two are invisible from `service-settings` and the engine's holder set is **not statically enumerable**.

I verified that independently on `origin/main` rather than taking the dev's word, and said so in the ACCEPT.

⇒ **First conjunct false ⇒ condition false ⇒ "the outcome is A regardless."** That is the ruling executing itself, not me re-adjudicating it.

### Timeline — the measurement predates the ruling by ~9 hours

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 01:20Z / 01:21Z | falsification posted on **this card**, twice, flagged provisional |
| 02:26Z | PR #8261 merged; falsification **reviewer-confirmed**; standing recommendation on this card amended to **A** |
| 10:04Z | ruling recorded as **B**, conditional |

### Two signs the ruling was recorded against a stale reading of this card

⚠️ Stating these as observations, ⛔ not as grounds to override anything:

1. **It says it is "accepting the card's own recommendation as presented"** — but the recommendation *as presented on this card* since 02:26Z has been **A**. The card **body** still reads "Recommendation: **B**, with A as the first release if #8103's measurements come back uncertain," because I amended by comment and never rewrote the body. A reader of the body alone would see B. **That is my process error, not the ruler's** — an amended recommendation that lives only in comments while the body still says something else is exactly the half-state this lane keeps filing findings about, and I created one.
2. **Its implementation note says "for when #8103 closes and the unlock scan re-prices this"** — implying #8103's measurements were still pending. They landed at 02:2xZ. #8103 is open only because its *deletion* half waits on **this** card; its *measurement* half shipped and was reviewed.

### What I am doing, and what I am not

- ⛔ **Not closing this card yet**, even though the A branch prescribes it. The ruling's premise about #8103's state looks stale, and closing a maintainer decision card on a technicality it may not have been aware of is the wrong direction of error when the maintainer is reachable. Flagged to them directly.
- ⛔ **Nothing destructive ships either way.** Under A no deletion is built; under B the deletion would be built only over the attributable subset after a three-producer reference union exists — which cannot be built from `service-settings`. **Both branches agree that nothing gets deleted this release**, so there is no urgency and no risk in taking one more exchange to get the record right.
- ✅ **Fixing my half now**: the card body's recommendation line is stale and will be corrected to match the amended one, so no future reader is handed B by a body that a comment overturned nine hours earlier.

### If the ruling stands as B knowingly

Then it activates only on the attributable subset, and the prerequisite is a runtime reference union spanning all three producers — a card that does **not** belong to `service-settings` (two of the three families are invisible there). That would need filing and routing before any deletion work could be dispatched. Saying so now so the path is visible either way.

Triage seat, state repair (maintainer-directed, 2026-08-13 live session — the maintainer flagged this card as an instance of "ruled/triaged but the state never moved"): **`pm:blocked` → `needs-user-decision`.**

Why this is the honest state right now, from the record above:
- The body's `Blocked-by: #8103` was **spent at 02:26Z** (PR #8261 merged; the measurement half this decision waited on is in and reviewed). A blocked state pointing at a discharged blocker is stale either way.
- The 10:04Z ruling (B, conditional) and the 13:45Z services-seat reading (the ruling's own condition had already failed at ruling time — reachability fact 2 was falsified and reviewer-confirmed at 02:26Z, so literal execution selects **A**) are in open contradiction, flagged to the maintainer by the seat. A card whose recorded ruling is contested-as-recorded-against-stale-state is a decision **pending**, not a decision made — `needs-user-decision` is the state that says so.

What resolves it — one line from the maintainer, two branches, both already fully specified on-card:
- **"A"** (the condition executes literally) ⇒ report-only ships; this card closes not-planned with the reason, per the ruling's own text.
- **"B, knowingly"** (condition waived, attributable-subset scope) ⇒ the prerequisite card (runtime three-producer reference union, NOT owned by `service-settings`) gets filed and routed first; this card goes `pm:blocked` against it — with a live blocker this time.

Process lesson extracted to the PM skill card #8449 (amendment 2): ruling-recording must be atomic — state transition + body/comments divergence check + Blocked-by liveness re-check in the same action.

## Maintainer ruling — **A** (report-only ships; no deletion is built this release)

Ruled in a live PM session, 2026-08-13, accepting the triage seat's four-prism recommendation in full (maintainer verbatim: 「接受你的全部建议」), with the recommendation presented to them as **A**. This supersedes the 10:04Z record of **B**, which was made against a stale reading of this card. Recorded by the triage seat as a ruling record.

**Ruling: A.** The read-only reporter/classifier that merged is what ships. ⛔ No deletion vehicle is built — not a migration, not an admin command, not an opt-in script. This is also what the earlier ruling's own condition selects when executed literally: its activation required re-establishing **the three** reachability facts, and fact 2 (`sys_setting.value_enc` is the only column holding a handle) was falsified and reviewer-confirmed nine hours before that ruling was recorded — three producers exist, two invisible from `service-settings`, one not statically enumerable.

Prism basis, as amended by measurement: the measurement inverted the urgency — for this population the value **still in force is the oldest one**, and the orphans hold values that never took effect, so deleting orphans does not retire the exposed credential; `orphaned` is a heuristic verdict on a table with no producer column, which makes **every** deleting option rest on it; and a wrong deletion is unrecoverable and un-nameable afterwards, because the audit trail records digests rather than handles.

**If this is ever revisited (option B, attributable subset only):** the prerequisite is a runtime reference union spanning all three producers, which ⛔ cannot be built from `service-settings` — that would be its own card, filed and routed first. Nothing about that is scheduled here.

**Record-hygiene note:** this card's BODY still reads "Recommendation: B, with A as the first release…". That line is **superseded** by the 02:26Z amendment and by this ruling. The body is deliberately left unedited — an MCP body round-trip risks entity-escaping corruption of the original text — so this comment is the authoritative correction for any future reader.

State: `needs-user-decision` → **closed, not planned**, per the ruling's own A branch. The body's `Blocked-by: #8103` was spent at 02:26Z and is discharged, not carried. Downstream: #8103 moves to `pm:on-hold` (its delivered half shipped; its destructive half is what this ruling declines) rather than closing, so the exposure stays on the record with restart conditions.
